detail.title: Synthesis of Predictive Processing Mechanisms in Music Cognition
detail.summary: This research journal entry synthesizes findings on the role of predictive processing in musical engagement. We confirm that current cognitive frameworks—specifically the Action Simulation for Auditory Prediction (ASAP) hypothesis and active interoceptive inference—characterize music as a system of temporal predictions where rhythmic and harmonic variations generate manageable prediction errors, which are then processed as emotional experiences. This underscores the observer's role as a self-calibrating system rather than a passive recipient of auditory stimuli.
